findings.reason: §17 must either name `landed_section_ids` as the extent owner to extend and have the parser read it, or state that the parser becomes the sole owner and `landed_section_ids` delegates to it; a forked card recogniser drifts from the writer that mints cards.
findings.text: §17 folds section identity and the replaced span into `_StructuredSectionSpanParser`, but the span it must yield for an already-landed section is the card, and card recognition stays in `_store.landed_section_ids` / `_landed_card_span` / `_is_structural_boundary` (`_store.py:992–1062`); §16 then consumes `landed_section_ids` for the fingerprint while §17's parser re-derives the same boundary, so one change set would carry two recognisers of a landed card

findings.reason: §16 must say which convention holds — make the predicate public and count it, or state why a module-private cross-package reader is acceptable where §18's is not — before its "no public definition is added" claim can be checked from the section text alone.
findings.text: §16 keeps the coverage predicate module-private so `public_definitions` stays flat, explicitly because its two consumers live in the same `reckon/crew` package, while §18 applies the opposite convention to the same situation — it hoists promotion's reader to a public name on `_store.py`, calling the public home "the price of a cross-module mechanism"; the two sections cannot both be the house rule, and the counts supplied for this week (public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23) show any public addition is a tracked family

findings.reason: the section must name the function that yields the per-section digests and the record key that holds them, or the node cannot write the record the coverage predicate of §16 then reads.
findings.text: §16 says the whole-document fingerprint becomes the digest of the sorted per-section digest set and that the stored record "carries the section digests beside that identity", and it also says the public `plan_fingerprint` signature deliberately does not widen; the record must therefore hold per-section digests but no interface is named that returns them, and `_authored_prose` is named only as gaining "the ability", not as a callable the composer (`reckon/crew/recovery.py:593`, which today calls only `plan_fingerprint(document)`) could use

findings.reason: the module already carries a module-private rule consumed only by a test (`_staged_writes`, `tests/test_staged_write_inventory.py`), so the placement follows an established in-repo pattern and the node can implement it as written.
findings.text: §17 adds a heading-walk reporting rule to the interface census whose only consumer is §17's own done-when (the head-vs-base site count); `interface_counts.counts` returns exactly the four counted families and a site-reporting rule is a different output shape

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §16 claims a per-section digest set without naming the interface that yields it, so the depth it describes has no surface a node can call.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §17 moves section-extent recognition into the raw-text parser while §16 keeps `_store.landed_section_ids` as the card recogniser, leaving the "this extent is a landed card" predicate with two owners and no statement of which the other delegates to.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 declares its coverage predicate module-private to hold public_definitions flat while §18 (same change set) hoists a cross-module reader to a public name on `_store.py`, so §16's "no public definition is added here" is not settled by its own text.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched the codebase it extends and cites the mechanisms it builds on; every one named above exists at the citation given.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §16's coverage predicate is justified against `read_plan_review` (one record to one digest) and §18 relocates an existing reader rather than wrapping it.
